title: UsageRecord
description: One line of a tool's usage log, which records the shape of one run and never the values of its arguments.

alias.description: Whether a personal alias expanded. It is present only when one did.

args.description:
The keyed hash of the words after the tool's name, so identical
command lines share a hash.

at.description:
When the run ended, in RFC 3339 with milliseconds, such as
2026-10-07T12:01:07.120Z.

code.description:
The code of the run's failure or refusal in the tool's spelling, such
as `shelf::books::not_found`. A batch gives the code of its first
failure.

command.description: The command path below the tool's name, such as books show.

empty.description:
Whether a listing or a stream had no rows, so its output printed the
empty note (ADR-0050). It is present only when one had none.

exit.description:
The exit code that `parse` or `finish` returned, or that the tool
reported with `events::ended`.

ext.description: The tool's own section, when the tool sets one.

flags.description:
The flags typed on the command line, each by its long name, or by its
short name when it has no long one, sorted.

help.description: short for -h, and long for --help or the help command.

ids.description:
How many values the command's positional arguments named ID received.
It is present only when the command has such an argument.

interrupted.description:
Whether the line was written when the run ended on SIGINT or SIGTERM.
It is present only when that is so.

ms.description: The run's wall time in milliseconds, from `start` to the line.

nearest.description: The real flag that clap suggested for a refused flag.

out_bytes.description:
The bytes that `finish` wrote to standard output, or that the tool
reported with `events::ended`.

parent.description:
The caller's span id from a valid TRACEPARENT. It is left out when the
run started a new trace.

picked.description:
How many missing arguments a picker filled in before the command line
parsed. It is present only when a picker filled one in.

run.description:
The run's own random span id, which its children name as their
parent.

schema.description:
The id of this record, `<tool>/usage/v1`, with the tool's name as
its component, such as shelf/usage/v1.

session.description:
The keyed hash of the agent's session id, or, when the agent gives no
session id, of the parent process id on Unix and of the Windows
Terminal session or the text `windows` on Windows.

tolerated.description:
The codes of the failures that the run met and recovered from, which
the tool reported with `events::tolerated`, in the tool's spelling.
Each code appears once, in report order, and the list holds at most
8 codes. It is present only when the tool reported one.

tool.description: The name of the tool's root command, such as shelf.

trace.description:
The id of the trace that the run belongs to: the caller's, from a
valid TRACEPARENT, or a new random id.

truncated.description:
Whether a listing showed fewer rows than its total. It is present only
when one did.

unknown_flags.description: How many flags of a refused command line name no flag of the command.

version.description: The tool's version, when its command has one.

Hash.description:
The keyed SipHash-2-4 hash of a list of byte strings, as 16 lowercase hex
digits.

Help.description: Which help page the caller asked for.

Name.description:
A name from the tool's own vocabulary: a command path, a flag, a version
or a failure code.

crumbkit reads every name from the tool's clap command tree or its codes,
and never from a word that the caller typed: each constructor takes a
`clap::Command`, a `clap::Arg` or a crumbkit `Code`.

Section.description:
The tool's own section of the record, which it sets with
`crumbkit_usage::section`.

data.description:
The section's fields. The tool owns them and keeps argument values out
of them, because crumbkit cannot check them.

schema.description: The id of the section's document, such as shelf/usage-ext/v1.

SpanId.description: A W3C span id, as 16 lowercase hex digits.

TraceId.description: A W3C trace id, as 32 lowercase hex digits.
